Reviewed the decision-0040 rework on slice-review-gates-chain (77c3099) across correctness, simplicity and SECURITY; the rework diff is b24110e..HEAD, confined to hands.rs, brokkr-cli, the v6 schema + contracts/README (additive only), docs/0040 + READMEs, and tests. The engine/bundle/agents/adapters wiring is unchanged from the accepted b24110e. Tree clean, no fixes applied.

Both first-review HIGH findings are genuinely closed:
- ~/.cargo persistence: the five review agents now bind ~/.cargo mode `overlay` (host is a read-only lower layer, all writes land in a per-seat upper layer under the session dir), rustup ro, credentials masked. box_argv emits `--overlay-src <host> --overlay <upper> <work> <host>` then the `--ro-bind /dev/null` masks for that same bind, so the credentials mask lands on top of the overlay. Proven by a real-box test: a boxed `echo evil > ~cargo/bin/cargo` is visible inside the box and on the next call of the same session, while the host file still reads `host cargo`. The persistence path out of the box is gone: nothing a boxed command writes to a toolchain cache reaches a program the operator later runs.
- git in a worktree: git_facts() reads --git-common-dir and user.name/email on the host before the box; a git worktree's common dir is bound rw so commits reach it, its `hooks` are an empty tmpfs and its `config` is read-only, identity flows via GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_*, and commit.gpgsign is forced false through GIT_CONFIG_*. Proven by a real-box Linux test: a boxed commit in a `git worktree` succeeds, unsigned, under the host identity and reaches the common dir; the hooks dir reads empty and a written hook never reaches the host; `git config --local core.hooksPath /evil` fails and the host config is unchanged. Hooks and config are the only host-executable persistence vectors in the common dir and both are masked; per-worktree config.worktree is inert without the extension, which the box cannot enable.

Lesser first-review findings all resolved: exec strips only the leading `--` (new test proves an inner `--` survives); output is bounded while draining via drain_bounded, which keeps OUTPUT_BYTES and discards the rest to EOF so host memory is bounded and the child never blocks on a full pipe; the env list and the codex native-shell exposure are named in 0040's ruling 1 and Consequences; refuse_unboxable hard-stops run/resume/rerun without bwrap, naming the seats (tested on empty PATH and with a planted bwrap).

The codex native-shell read exposure remains a documented, operator-accepted consequence, not an open finding: on the sol link codex's own read-only shell still sees the whole host, so the box governs writes only there. The task's accepted scope required exactly this naming in Consequences, and the doc now states the boundary honestly (cannot-see-host holds for Claude Code and exec; for codex, writes only). Not a regression — these agents ran fully unboxed before — and read-only egress remains decision 0036's axis.
